properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued October 19 at 9:53PM AKDT until October 20 at 10:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Snow expected. Total snow accumulations between 6 and 12
inches, highest amounts above 2000 feet elevation.

* WHERE...Anchorage and Eagle River Hillsides.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM AKDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult. Be prepared for slippery
roads. Areas of low visibility especially in heavier snow.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Rain and snow this evening will transition to
all snow by late this evening, then continue through late Tuesday
evening. The heaviest snow will be Tuesday morning through around
midday.
properties.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. For the latest road
conditions call 5 1 1 or visit 511.alaska.gov.

NWSheadline: WINTER WEATHER ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 10 PM AKDT TUESDAY

properties.description:
* WHAT...Snow expected. Total snow accumulations between 6 and 12
inches. Highest amounts between Eureka and Sheep Mountain.

* WHERE...Eureka, Tahneta Pass and the Western Copper Valley.

* WHEN...Until 4 AM AKDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult. Be prepared for slippery

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Occasional light snow today will give way to
steadier snowfall this evening through Tuesday evening before
slowly tapering off by Wednesday morning. The heaviest snow is
expected to fall between early Tuesday morning and Tuesday evening.
Up to 6 inches of snow is expected around Mendeltna with higher
amounts farther west along the Glenn Highway.
properties.instruction:

properties.areaDesc: Anchorage; Lower Matanuska Valley; Sutton / Upper Matanuska Valley
properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued October 19 at 9:53PM AKDT until October 20 at 1:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Snow expected. Total snow accumulations between 2 and 6
inches, highest amounts near the mountains.

* WHERE...Lower elevations of Anchorage and the Matanuska Valley.

* WHEN...From 4 AM to 1 PM AKDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult. Be prepared for slippery
roads. Visibilities as low as one half mile possible, including
during the morning commute.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Rain will intensify during the overnight hours
and change to  snow late tonight through early Tuesday morning,
with temperatures falling to near freezing. The heaviest snow and
highest accumulation will be near the mountains, from the lower
Anchorage Hillside to East Anchorage and up the Glenn Highway
corridor to Palmer and Sutton. Roads will start out wet and road
surface temperatures are still warm (in the upper 30s), but steady
moderate snow should be enough to lead to slushy accumulation,
especially along neighborhood roads. Snow will change back to rain
by late morning in south to west Anchorage, continue northward to
the Matanuska Valley in the afternoon. The exact timing of
changeover back to rain will greatly impact total snow amounts.
properties.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. For the latest road
conditions call 5 1 1 or visit 511.alaska.gov.
